episode_title: Från finans till fastigheter: USAs småbolag under lupp

recommendations.speaker: Geoff Davies
recommendations.reasoning: Small caps trading at one of the deepest discounts to large caps in history. Catalysts include narrowing earnings growth gap, fiscal stimulus (tax benefits, deregulation), banking deregulation providing more liquidity, and multi-year reshoring theme bringing manufacturing back to US. Small caps more exposed to domestic-focused sectors like industrials, financials, cyclical areas which will benefit from improved economy and domestic investment.
recommendations.quote: US small caps are now trading at one of the deepest discounts to large caps... we do see signs and signals in catalysts that would narrow that gap, where small cap valuations catch up to large cap... a lot of it's going to be predicated on the narrowing of the earnings growth gap.

recommendations.speaker: Geoff Davies
recommendations.reasoning: Dynamic and innovative sector with many idiosyncratic ideas. Strong M&A catalyst: large pharma companies facing huge patent cliffs losing hundreds of billions in revenue by 2030, need to replace revenue by acquiring small cap biotechs. Pharma companies have great balance sheets, lots of cash, can access debt markets. Biotech takeout premiums can be 50-100% providing quick alpha. Six companies acquired from their fund this year, expect more in 2026.
recommendations.quote: One that we've liked is health care... particularly in the biotech and med tech space, we're finding great ideas... Biotech in particular is interesting because you have these large pharmaceutical companies that have very big patent cliffs... they have to replace that revenue stream... They're going to acquire a number of small cap biotech companies

recommendations.speaker: Geoff Davies
recommendations.reasoning: Banks levered to local markets like Southeast where there's new plants from automakers, job growth, and population growth. Demographic shifts showing people moving to Southeast since COVID. Can get exposure to specific regional growth through select small cap companies instead of large caps levered to entire nation. Banking deregulation allowing more liquidity and lending.
recommendations.quote: You can get a bank that's levered to a local market... levered to the southeast where there's new plants going in from automakers... there's just going to be more job growth there... allows them to bank more customers.

recommendations.speaker: Geoff Davies
recommendations.reasoning: Owns office suite investing in premier office space in 'smile' region (southwest to Texas to southeast). Exposure to growthier US markets with class A properties, high amenities. Post-COVID trend: companies upgrading office space despite hybrid work. Highest quality properties getting highest rents and best occupancy. Value play held from couple years ago.
recommendations.quote: We own an office suite that invests in premier office space in what they call the smile... they have exposure to more of the growthier markets... they do that with class A properties, with high amenities properties that are really gaining share since COVID.

recommendations.speaker: Geoff Davies
recommendations.reasoning: Companies providing NAND storage for increased bandwidth/data from AI. Optical networking connecting data centers. Industrials doing liquid cooling within data centers. Asset managers catering to digital investments. However, very cognizant of valuations - actively managing position sizes and trimming back winners. Recycling AI winners into software losers potentially disrupted by AI. Some speculation and frothiness in AI-related small caps.
recommendations.quote: There's a lot of AI infrastructure plays down market cap that are very interesting... companies that are providing NAND storage... optical networking company that connects data centers... industrials that are doing liquid cooling within data centers... we're very cognizant of valuations... actively managing those position sizes and trimming them back.

bull_case: Valuation discount to large caps at historical levels

Fiscal stimulus with tax benefits for domestic investment
Deregulation improving permitting and banking liquidity

summary: US small caps trading at deepest discount to large caps in history. Guest sees narrowing discount over next year driven by earnings growth gap narrowing, fiscal stimulus, deregulation, and reshoring. Favorite sectors: healthcare/biotech (strong M&A catalyst from pharma patent cliffs), regional banks (southeast growth), and selective AI infrastructure. Maintains disciplined valuation awareness, actively trimming AI winners.
key_takeaways: Small cap valuation discount to large caps at historic levels creates opportunity
Healthcare/biotech: M&A catalyst as pharma faces hundreds of billions in patent cliffs by 2030
Reshoring and domestic stimulus supporting industrials, financials, cyclicals
Southeast regional markets benefiting from demographic shifts and business-friendly environment
AI infrastructure opportunities in small cap (storage, networking, cooling) but valuations being watched carefully
Active portfolio management: recycling AI winners into software losers potentially disrupted by AI
